sentences.text:
According to the terms of settlement, the petitioner No.1 is to remit to respondent No.2 a sum of Rs.33,00,000/- as full and final settlement against stridhan and dowry, maintenance towards past,
present and future by way of three instalments.
6. It is jointly submitted by learned counsel appearing for the parties that the entire sum of Rs.33,00,000/- already stands tendered to the respondent No.2.
7. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2 on instructions submits that respondent No.2 has received the entire amount.

8. In terms of the settlement, the passport of the minor child has already been handed over by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners to learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2,
who affirms the same.

9. According to the terms of settlement, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the last instalment of Rs.13,00,000/- was agreed to be converted into the FDR in the name of minor child to be kept for his benefit.

10. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2 on instructions submits that the said terms has been complied with and as on date there is already an FDR of Rs.13,00,000/- in the name of This is a digitally signed order.

11. IO is present and identifies the parties present in Court.
12. In terms of the settlement, the parties have dissolved their marriage by way of decree of divorce under the provisions of Section 13(B) of the HMA, 1955.
Copy of the decree dated 17.07.2023 dissolving the said marriage between the parties is placed at page 48 of the present petition.
13. Notwithstanding the terms of settlement, the independent legal rights of minor child shall remain unaffected and reserved in accordance with law.
14. This Court has interacted with the respondent No.2 who affirms that the entire sum of Rs.33,00,000/- in accordance with the terms of settlement.
She also submits that in pursuance of the terms of settlement, a sum of Rs.13,00,000/- have already been converted into the FDR in the name of minor child.
She submits that she has no further claims against the petitioners and she has no objection in case the present FIR is quashed.
